questions.q: What is the main difference between FI and CO?
options: FI is the official books for outsiders; CO is the internal view of costs and profit for managers
FI is for sales; CO is for purchasing
FI is only used in Denmark; CO is used everywhere
FI handles salaries; CO handles bank statements
questions.reason: FI (Financial Accounting) produces the balance sheet, P&L and VAT return for authorities, auditors and owners. CO (Controlling) shows managers which department or product costs or earns what.

questions.q: Jonas Krogh wants to know whether tables or chairs make more money. Which part of FICO answers that?
options: CO, using profit centres such as PC-TABLES and PC-CHAIRS
FI, using the VAT return
The bank statement
The chart of accounts alone
questions.reason: Profit per product is an internal, management question. CO answers it with profit centres and margin analysis.

questions.q: Who are the main readers of FI reports such as the balance sheet and P&L?
options: Authorities, auditors, banks and owners
Only the warehouse team
Only the IT department
Customers checking their invoices
questions.reason: FI looks outward: its reports follow law and accounting standards and are read by people outside the company's management.

questions.q: Why does a FICO BA need to understand other modules such as MM and SD?
options: Most FI and CO postings are created automatically by events in those modules
Because FI cannot post anything by itself
Because MM and SD replace FI in S/4HANA
Because FICO has no GL accounts of its own
questions.reason: Goods receipts, billing, payroll and bank statements all create postings in FI and CO, so the cause of a number often starts in another module.

questions.q: What is a company code?
options: One legal company with its own balance sheet and P&L, such as DK01
A password for logging on to SAP
A cost centre for the head office
The number of a supplier
questions.reason: The company code is the smallest unit that must produce full legal accounts. Nordlys Møbler A/S is company code DK01.

questions.q: What is the client in SAP?
options: The top level: one SAP installation's set of data that holds everything else
A customer who buys tables
A cost centre for sales
A type of journal entry
questions.reason: The client (for example 100) sits above company codes and controlling areas. In everyday English 'client' can mean customer, but in SAP it means this top level.

questions.q: What is a chart of accounts such as NMKP?
options: The list of all GL accounts a company code may use
A diagram of the company's departments
The list of open posting periods
A bank's list of transactions
questions.reason: The chart of accounts is like a dictionary of where money can be recorded, for example 110000 Bank or 470000 Rent.

questions.q: Nordlys Møbler uses a calendar fiscal year with 12 normal periods and 4 special periods. What are the special periods for?
options: Year-end corrections after December, without reopening December
Extra months for leap years
Postings in foreign currency
Payroll only
questions.reason: Special periods 13 to 16 hold year-end adjustments such as audit corrections, so December stays clean but the annual figures include them.

questions.q: Which transaction is used to open and close posting periods?
options: OB52
FB03
FS00
FBL3N
questions.reason: OB52 controls which periods are open. If period 3 is closed, a posting dated in March is refused.

questions.q: What is the relationship between controlling area NM00 and company code DK01?
options: DK01 is assigned to NM00; a controlling area can hold several company codes
NM00 is a GL account inside DK01
They are two names for the same thing
NM00 is the bank account of DK01
questions.reason: The controlling area is the unit in which CO works. Company codes are assigned to it, and one controlling area can contain several company codes.

questions.q: What is a cost centre?
options: A place where costs happen and someone is responsible, usually a department such as 3000 Administration
A product line you want a profit figure for
A bank account
A type of supplier invoice
questions.reason: Cost centres collect costs by responsibility. Nordlys Møbler has 1000 Production Aarhus, 2000 Sales, 3000 Administration and 4100 IT.

questions.q: What is a profit centre?
options: A part of the business you want a profit figure for, such as PC-TABLES
A department that only has costs, never revenue
A GL account for revenue
The bank where profits are kept
questions.reason: Profit centres show profit by product line, region or business unit. Nordlys Møbler uses PC-TABLES and PC-CHAIRS.

questions.q: Which kinds of account go UP with a debit?
options: Assets and expenses
Liabilities and revenue
Equity and revenue
Liabilities and equity
questions.reason: Assets (such as the bank) and expenses (such as rent) increase on the debit side. Liabilities, equity and revenue increase on the credit side.

questions.q: How does SAP usually show a credit amount in line item reports?
options: As a negative number, so every document adds up to 0.00
As a positive number in red
It does not show credits at all
As a percentage
questions.reason: Debits are positive and credits negative. The bank line of the rent document shows -50,000.00, and the document balances to 0.00.

questions.q: What happens to a P&L account such as 470000 Rent at the end of the year?
options: Its total moves into equity (retained earnings) and it starts again from zero
Its balance carries forward to the next year unchanged
It is deleted from the chart of accounts
It becomes a balance sheet account
questions.reason: P&L accounts measure one period. The year's profit or loss goes to retained earnings; balance sheet accounts such as the bank carry their balance forward.

questions.q: Why can Maria not post directly to account 160000 Trade payables?
options: It is a reconciliation account, updated only through postings to suppliers
It is closed in OB52
It belongs to the controlling area only
It is a P&L account
questions.reason: A reconciliation account summarises a group of suppliers or customers. Posting to the supplier (such as Jysk Træ) updates 160000 automatically, so the GL always agrees with the supplier list.

questions.q: In the FB03 screen, what do posting keys 40 and 50 mean?
options: 40 is a debit to a GL account, 50 is a credit to a GL account
40 is a customer invoice, 50 is a supplier invoice
40 and 50 are cost centre numbers
40 means posted, 50 means reversed
questions.reason: Posting keys say whether a line is a debit or a credit and what kind of account it is. 40 and 50 are the GL account debit and credit keys.

questions.q: The rent invoice is dated 25.02.2026 and posted on 01.03.2026. Which month does the cost count in?
options: March, because the posting date decides the period
February, because the document date decides the period
Both months, half each
Neither, until it is paid
questions.reason: The posting date decides the period. 01.03.2026 falls in period 3 (March). The document date is the date on the original paper.

questions.q: What does document type SA stand for in the rent example?
options: A plain GL account document
A sales invoice to a customer
A supplier invoice
An asset posting
questions.reason: SA is used for general GL account postings such as the rent payment. Supplier invoices typically use KR, customer invoices DR and asset postings AA.

questions.q: In the rent document, why does the line for 470000 Rent have cost centre 3000, but the bank line has none?
options: Rent is a cost, so CO needs to know which department carries it; a bank account is not a cost
Bank lines are never shown in FB03
Cost centre 3000 only exists for the bank
It is a mistake that must be corrected
questions.reason: Cost lines need a cost object for CO. Balance sheet lines such as the bank do not.

questions.q: How do you correct a posted journal entry that was wrong?
options: Post a reversal document; the original is never deleted
Delete it in FB03
Change the amount in FS10N
Close the period in OB52
questions.reason: Posted documents are permanent. A reversal posts the opposite signs and the original is marked as reversed, so the audit trail stays complete.

questions.q: What is the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA) in S/4HANA?
options: One table where every posting line is stored with both its FI and CO information
A separate CO table that must be reconciled with FI every month
A list of all users who posted documents
A Fiori app for printing invoices
questions.reason: In S/4HANA every line item lands in ACDOCA with company code, GL account, amount, cost centre, profit centre and more, so FI and CO cannot disagree.

questions.q: In S/4HANA, where do you maintain a cost element such as Rent?
options: In FS00, as a GL account with a cost element category
In OB52
In FB03
In a separate CO-only master that has no GL account
questions.reason: In S/4HANA cost elements are GL accounts. FS00 holds the cost element category, primary (like rent) or secondary (like 940000 IT assessment).

questions.q: In the March example, total debits are DKK 323,000. What must total credits be?
options: DKK 0
questions.reason: In double entry every posting balances, so the total of all debits always equals the total of all credits.

questions.q: In the March example, why is the DKK 80,000 of oak not counted as a cost yet?
options: It sits in the warehouse as an asset until it is used to make tables
Because VAT was added
Because the supplier has not been paid
Because oak is never a cost
questions.reason: Raw materials are an asset (account 200000) while in stock. They become a cost (raw material consumption) when used in production.

questions.q: What is the March profit so far in the example (revenue minus rent, electricity and depreciation)?
questions.reason: Revenue 120,000 minus rent 50,000, electricity 18,000 and depreciation 5,000 gives DKK 47,000.

questions.q: Which transaction shows a GL account's balance period by period, for example how much rent was posted so far this year?
options: FS10N
FB50
OB52
FS00
questions.reason: FS10N shows GL account balances per period. FBL3N shows the individual line items behind them.
